title: Introduction to design intent in Fusion
creator: Autodesk
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with the Fusion interface; no engineering mathematics required.
access: Public self-paced learning module; Fusion software access is separate.
why: A compact starting point for understanding what a model should preserve when dimensions change.
first_task: Complete the module, then identify one hardware-driven dimension and one freely chosen dimension in your sensor mount.
limitations: Thirteen-minute introduction, not a complete CAD course or manufacturing validation method.
evidence_note: Opened official module page; verified duration, fully defined sketches, parameters, and parts/assemblies objectives.

title: Fusion sketch constraints
creator: Autodesk
prerequisites: Ability to create and edit a sketch in Fusion.
access: Public nine-minute Autodesk tutorial; software license separate.
why: Pairs well with a deliberate drag test so geometric freedom becomes visible rather than abstract.
first_task: Constrain two equal mounting holes symmetrically about an origin; explain every constraint you add.
limitations: Interface details may differ by version; a fully constrained sketch can still encode an incorrect measurement.
evidence_note: Opened official tutorial page and verified its stated purpose and nine-minute length.

title: Modeling with 3D printing in mind
creator: Prusa Research
prerequisites: Ability to inspect a solid model and slicer preview.
why: Connects geometric decisions to the manufacturing process, especially useful before adding decorative-looking edge treatments.
first_task: Compare two orientations of a small mount and annotate support access, critical surfaces, and a purposeful chamfer.
limitations: General guidelines do not establish fit allowances or strength for a specific printer and material.
evidence_note: Opened official article; verified sections on orientation, overhangs, fillet versus chamfer, thin walls, tolerances, and iteration.

title: Layers and perimeters
creator: Prusa Research
prerequisites: A model open in a slicer; basic understanding of layers.
why: Explains the controls that turn a solid volume into shells and layers, making preview inspection more purposeful.
first_task: Change only perimeter count and compare the same narrow section in both toolpath previews.
limitations: Written for PrusaSlicer; Bambu Studio terminology and available controls can differ. Do not copy machine profiles blindly.
evidence_note: Opened official documentation and checked layer-height, perimeter, thin-wall, and solid-layer sections.

title: Filament Material Guide
creator: Prusa Research
prerequisites: An intended application and knowledge of your printer's hardware.
why: Useful for screening materials against environment and processing needs before investigating a specific filament datasheet.
first_task: Compare two candidates for an indoor mount, recording hardware compatibility and the evidence still missing for creep.
limitations: General material families and printer-oriented settings do not certify a printed part's service performance.
evidence_note: Opened official guide; verified comparison categories for hardware, temperatures, build surfaces, and physical/application characteristics.

title: Bambu Studio
creator: Bambu Lab
prerequisites: A supported desktop computer and a small model to slice; printer optional for preview work.
access: Open-source application with official prebuilt releases; some networking functionality uses an optional separate plugin.
why: The immediate practice environment for the handbook's X1 Carbon reader, including layer and G-code inspection.
first_task: Open a fit coupon, confirm its dimensions, and compare flat and edge orientations without printing.
limitations: The repository is a software source and release entry point, not a complete beginner curriculum. Profile choice remains machine-specific.
evidence_note: Opened manufacturer repository README; verified desktop releases, slicing/G-code viewer, support types, and project capabilities. Manufacturer wiki fetch failed, so it is not used as verification evidence.

title: Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, sixth edition
creator: Michael F. Ashby; Elsevier
prerequisites: Basic mechanics, algebra, and willingness to work with property charts; later methods are more mathematical.
access: Paid print/e-book; library access may be available.
why: Develops a defensible way to compare material, shape, process, and competing objectives rather than choosing by a single strength number.
first_task: Read selection basics and make a three-candidate decision table for the sensor mount.
limitations: Broad engineering text; not a spool-specific FDM calibration guide. Publisher listing has differing publication-date fields, so no exact release date is asserted here.
evidence_note: Opened publisher listing; verified author, sixth edition, and contents on properties, selection, processes, shape, and environment.

title: 2.008 Design and Manufacturing II, Spring 2025
creator: MIT OpenCourseWare; Jung-Hoon Chun and Josh Ramos
prerequisites: Prior mechanical design experience; original course lists MIT 2.007 as prerequisite.
access: Free archived lecture notes, assignments, and project materials; not live enrollment, certification, or shop access.
why: Extends one-off making into tradeoffs involving production rate, quality, cost, and process capability.
first_task: Review the process overview and compare printing, machining, and purchased stock for five identical brackets.
limitations: The original integrated shop experience is not reproduced by reading the archive; some exercises require university equipment.
evidence_note: Opened official course page and inspected syllabus/calendar results; verified instructors, 2025 offering, notes, assignments, and project scope. A later repeated fetch was transiently unsuccessful.

title: 3.032 Mechanical Behavior of Materials, Fall 2007
creator: MIT OpenCourseWare; John Vander Sande and Krystyn van Vliet
prerequisites: Introductory mechanics and materials science; calculus helps with derivations and problems.
access: Free archived notes, problem sets/solutions, and exams; no live instruction or certificate.
why: Explains why materials deform and fail, supporting a deeper understanding of time, temperature, and microstructure effects.
first_task: Read the stress–strain and elasticity material, then distinguish stiffness, yield, and fracture in a sample curve.
limitations: Not a beginner printing course; listed laboratory activities are not instructions for unsupervised home testing.
evidence_note: Opened official course page; verified instructors, undergraduate level, resources, and elasticity/plasticity/creep/fracture scope.

title: 2.001 Mechanics & Materials I, Fall 2006
creator: MIT OpenCourseWare; Carol Livermore, Henrik Schmidt, James H. Williams, and Simona Socrate
prerequisites: Original syllabus expects classical mechanics and multivariable calculus, with differential equations as a corequisite.
access: Free archived lecture notes and problem sets; not a complete live or video course.
why: Develops the relationship between forces, geometry, deformation, and material behavior beyond isolated formulas.
first_task: Work a simple equilibrium problem before using the bending notes to reproduce the handbook's cantilever example.
limitations: Mathematical prerequisites are substantial; beginner readers should start with the statics text and handbook labs.
evidence_note: Opened official course page and reviewed syllabus result; verified named instructors, resource types, scope, and prerequisites.

title: Engineering Statics: Open & Interactive
creator: Daniel Baker, William Haynes, and contributing engineering faculty
prerequisites: Algebra, geometry, and basic trigonometry; work through vectors if rusty.
access: Free online open textbook and downloadable PDF.
why: Interactive figures make force directions and equilibrium easier to interrogate than a static formula sheet.
first_task: Study free-body diagrams and moments, then solve the two-support overhung-load example without looking at the answer.
limitations: Statics establishes equilibrium; material failure, dynamics, and manufactured-part validation require additional work.
evidence_note: Opened author project page; verified free online/PDF access, authorship background, and topics including equilibrium, structures, and area moments.

title: Engineering Mechanics: Statics video playlist
creator: Daniel Baker / DrDanTeaches
prerequisites: Algebra and basic geometry; use the companion text for notation.
access: Public YouTube playlist linked by the author's textbook site; platform access may vary.
why: Provides a visual companion for readers who benefit from seeing a diagram developed step by step.
first_task: Choose a moments or equilibrium lesson, pause before the solution, and draw your own free-body diagram.
limitations: Playlist landing page was accessible but the full set of videos was not watched or audited. Watching without solving is insufficient practice.
evidence_note: Verified the playlist's official author-site link and opened its YouTube landing page.

title: Haas and Autodesk Fusion: Blueprints, CAD, CAM, and CNC
creator: Autodesk and Haas
prerequisites: Basic Fusion modeling; machine-specific training and supervision for physical operations.
access: Public self-paced course with downloads; software and machine access separate.
why: Connects drawings and CAM to setup and inspection instead of treating toolpath generation as the complete workflow.
first_task: Use the blueprint and CAM-setup sections to make a paper stock, datum, and inspection plan without running machine code.
limitations: Haas-oriented examples do not establish compatibility with another controller or qualify an untrained operator.
evidence_note: Opened official course page; verified eleven-hour scope, setup/safety/inspection objectives, and downloadable drawings, exercises, and datasets.

title: Milling formulas and definitions
creator: Sandvik Coromant
prerequisites: Units, multiplication, and an understanding of cutter diameter, teeth, and spindle rotation.
why: An authoritative definitions page for checking feed-rate and cutting-speed arithmetic and avoiding unit confusion.
first_task: Reproduce the handbook's hypothetical 6 mm cutter example, showing all units before canceling them.
limitations: Formulas do not select appropriate cutting conditions or validate workholding; use tool-specific data and trained supervision.
evidence_note: Opened official reference; verified metric formulas for feed, cutting speed, spindle speed, and feed per tooth.
